panelRectification.method: Projective rectification from screen corners to the documented 9.07:5.44 aspect ratio, followed by uniform meter calibration. Wide-angle lens distortion and curved coaming remain.

corrections: Individual dimensioned H125 shell, curved windscreen and lower observation glazing, real roof apertures, asymmetric access layout, high skids and steps.
Arriel cowling and exhaust, three-blade Starflex-style head, tapering boom and swept fin built against exterior reference projections.
TXi/VEMD cockpit layout placed from rectified Airbus photograph using documented GDU 1060 screen dimensions; paired engine screens, round standby, warning matrix, console, controls and six seats.
Overlay and cockpit iterations corrected front skid support position, windshield/panel interference, unsupported console and opaque skylight placeholders.
limitations: Airbus dimension sheet uses rendered views with small front/side scale differences and different rotor azimuth. Printed dimensions take precedence; body curvature remains polygonal.
Panel rectification assumes a flat instrument face and identified GDU 1060 screen. Wide-angle lens distortion, curved coaming depth and absolute cabin installation remain approximate.
Cockpit follows the current TXi equipment fit; 2020 dimension sheet and related AS350 B3 exterior photo corroborate the shell. Optional avionics and mission fittings vary.
Displays are original simplified geometry and assisted-flight indicators, not certified avionics. Source images are research-only and are not distributed.

controlReview.checks: Imported GLB control-point movement tested at positive and negative commands; all 20 aircraft pass. Cockpit pairs and all ten airplane exterior pairs visually inspected. Roll, pitch, rudder and declared pedal directions corrected; ailerons and full flap deployment corrected.
limitations: Checks cover existing bindings; Cherokee and Caravan pedal geometry is static.
Full control travel and flight response remain approximations unless independently dimensioned in the model reference notes.
This audit verifies movement; it does not upgrade legacy helicopter avionics or remove previously documented geometry limitations.
